newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields higher as futures stalled.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields higher as futures stalled.

text.p: *Australian bond yields edged higher with the futures market running into resistance just after the opening and with little physical trade evident.
*March housing finance due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields edged higher with the futures market running into resistance just after the opening and with little physical trade evident.
The June 10-year bond futures contract walked into a wall of resistance at 92.340, an area the market flirted with on Friday and levels not seen late February.

"The market got smacked down at the opening, but there hasn't been any real (physical) flows to give a clue of outright direction at this stage," one trader said. "The fall on the (U.S.) dollar hasn't had a direct impact as yet."
The U.S. dollar dropped sharply in early Asian trading.
The U.S. dollar continued Friday's sell-off tumbling to a four-month low of 118 yen on aggressive Japanese selling.

The fall in the U.S. unit took the edge off a rally in U.S. Treasuries on Friday which followed remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and were seen by some as hinting that the Fed may not hike rates later this month.
Locally, the key event will be Tuesday's 1997/98 Federal budget, which is expected to be market-friendly, not least because little or no net bond issuance is likely to be projected, analysts said.

The local market slightly underperformed against the U.S. in early trading ahead of the Tokyo opening. Canadian debt rallied strongly on Friday on fading fears of a U.S. tightening, while short dated New Zealand bond yields rose today after the RBNZ said it would prefer to see monetary conditions firm somewhat.
